items.title: Finite modal velocity fields inherit finite second moments
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $(D,\mathcal D,\lambda)$, $d\ge1$, and $H=L^2(D,\lambda;\mathbb R^d)$ be as in the Definition of the finite-second-moment random velocity sensor law, with $0<\lambda(D)<\infty$. Let $m\ge1$, choose $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_m\in H$, and let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space. Suppose $A:(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal B(\mathbb R^m))$ is measurable and $\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}|A|^2<\infty$. Define $T:\mathbb R^m\to H$ by $T(a)=\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\phi_j$, set $U=T\circ A$, and define $\mu(B)=\mathbb P(U^{-1}(B))$ for every $B\in\mathcal B(H)$. Then $U$ is strongly measurable, $\mu$ is a probability measure on $(H,\mathcal B(H))$, and
$$\int_H\|v\|_H^2\,d\mu(v)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\|U\|_H^2\le\left(\sum_{j=1}^m\|\phi_j\|_H^2\right)\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}|A|^2<\infty.$$
items.axiom_use: Assume AC only to apply the Riesz-Fischer completeness theorem to the scalar coordinate spaces, whose proof uses countable choice to select measurable representatives. The finite direct-sum argument and the remaining local estimates use no additional choice.

references.title: Terence Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory, Section 1.4, Exercise 1.4.38 and Theorem 1.4.44
references.locator: Exercise 1.4.38, printed pp. 103–104, poses the pushforward-measure integral identity; Theorem 1.4.44, printed pp. 107–108, and its proof give monotone convergence. The pushforward identity is proved locally here.

items.title: Finite-modal fluid observation and noise model
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $E$ be a three-dimensional oriented Euclidean affine space. Fix an orientation-preserving affine isometry $x:E\to\mathbb R^3$ as the Cartesian inertial chart on Newtonian spacetime $I\times E$, with absolute time $t$ in seconds and spatial position in metres. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable observation region with volume $0<|D|<\infty$, and let $\mathcal H=L^2(D;\mathbb R^3)$ be the space of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of square-integrable vector fields, with norm $\|v\|_{\mathcal H}=(\int_D|v(x)|^2\,d^3x)^{1/2}$. Write $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ for the sigma-algebra generated by the norm-open sets. A velocity field has units m s$^{-1}$.

Choose an integer observation horizon $T\ge0$ and times $t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_T$ in $I$, where observations are taken at $t_1,\ldots,t_T$. For each $0\le k\le T$, let $m_k\ge1$ and choose dimensionless modal fields $\phi_{k,1},\ldots,\phi_{k,m_k}\in\mathcal H$. Define the modal map $\Phi_k:\mathbb R^{m_k}\to\mathcal H$ by $\Phi_k(a)=\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}a_j\phi_{k,j}$. The coefficient vector $a_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k}$ has units m s$^{-1}$, with initial mean $\mu_0$ in m s$^{-1}$, and its represented velocity field is $U_k=\Phi_k(a_k)$. This finite-dimensional representation is an adopted approximation for the selected observation times; it does not assert that an untruncated fluid field lies in one of these finite-dimensional spaces.

For each $1\le k\le T$, choose $p_k\ge1$ sensor weights $\psi_{k,1},\ldots,\psi_{k,p_k}\in\mathcal H$, with units m$^{-3}$. The ideal sensor on a field $v\in\mathcal H$ is the weighted spatial average $S_{\psi_{k,i}}(v)=\int_D v(x)\cdot\psi_{k,i}(x)\,d^3x$; it is not a point evaluation. Define $L_k:\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{k,1},\ldots,\phi_{k,m_k}\}\to\mathbb R^{p_k}$ by $(L_kv)_i=S_{\psi_{k,i}}(v)$ and define the dimensionless observation matrix by $[H_k]_{ij}=(L_k\phi_{k,j})_i$. Thus $L_k(U_k)=H_ka_k$, and each datum and observation-noise component has units m s$^{-1}$.

On a common probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$, adopt the finite linear-Gaussian coefficient model
$$a_0\sim N_{m_0}(\mu_0,P_0),\qquad a_k=F_ka_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad y_k=H_ka_k+r_k\quad(1\le k\le T),$$
where $\mu_0\in\mathbb R^{m_0}$, $P_0\in\mathbb R^{m_0\times m_0}$, $Q_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times m_k}$, and $R_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times p_k}$; $F_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times m_{k-1}}$ is dimensionless, $q_k\sim N_{m_k}(0,Q_k)$ has coefficient units m s$^{-1}$, and $r_k\sim N_{p_k}(0,R_k)$ has observation units m s$^{-1}$. The vectors $a_0,q_1,r_1,\ldots,q_T,r_T$ are mutually independent. Here $N_d(\mu,C)$ denotes the $d$-dimensional Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and covariance $C$, including singular covariance. A symmetric matrix $C$ is positive semidefinite, written $C\succeq0$, if $z^TCz\ge0$ for every vector $z$ of the matching dimension. The covariance matrices $P_0,Q_k,R_k$ have this property, with entries carrying the corresponding squared units. Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the Gaussian-law construction. The finite-dimensional Gaussian laws and their common probability-space realization use this assumption. For each $k$, define the field law by $\mu_k(B)=\mathbb P(U_k\in B)$ for $B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$; finite modal fields with finite-second-moment coefficients have finite-second-moment laws.

These linearity, Gaussianity, independence, covariance, finite-mode, and ideal-sensor conditions are adopted physical-model assumptions for this selected regime. The sensor weights and covariance matrices are model inputs; no calibration procedure is asserted. These conditions report no measurements and do not assert that an actual flow, observation system, or noise source satisfies them. Biased or temporally correlated errors, nonlinear observation maps, and untruncated fluid dynamics require separately stated models.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC only for the Gaussian-law construction specified by the finite linear-Gaussian supplier. The sensor maps and finite modal estimates use no additional choice principle.

items.physical_scope: Adopted discrete-time model for specified ideal weighted spatial velocity sensors applied to a finite-dimensional modal representation of a three-dimensional fluid velocity field in a fixed nonrelativistic Cartesian inertial chart. Gaussian initial-state, process-noise, and observation-noise assumptions are part of this selected model regime; no actual sensor calibration, universal fluid law, nonlinear or untruncated flow model, or empirical validity is asserted.

items.title: Exact conditional law for the finite-modal fluid filter
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function, and the finite-modal observation model described here. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $E$ be a three-dimensional oriented Euclidean affine space, and use an orientation-preserving Cartesian inertial chart $x:E\to\mathbb R^3$ with absolute time $t$. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable with $0<|D|<\infty$, and set $\mathcal H=L^2(D;\mathbb R^3)$, with its norm topology and Borel sigma-algebra. Fix an integer horizon $T\ge0$ and times $t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_T$ in $I$, positive integer dimensions $m_k,p_k$, finite-dimensional modal maps $\Phi_k(a)=\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}a_j\phi_{k,j}$ with $\phi_{k,j}\in\mathcal H$, and weighted sensor maps $L_k$ given by $(L_kv)_i=\int_Dv(x)\cdot\psi_{k,i}(x)\,d^3x$ for weights $\psi_{k,i}\in\mathcal H$. Assign $\phi_{k,j}$ dimensionless units, coefficients and velocity fields units m s$^{-1}$, sensor weights units m$^{-3}$, and observations and sensor noise units m s$^{-1}$; then $F_k$ and $H_k$ are dimensionless. The coefficient observation matrices satisfy $[H_k]_{ij}=(L_k\phi_{k,j})_i$, so $L_k(\Phi_k(a))=H_ka$.

On a common probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$, let $a_0\sim N_{m_0}(\mu_0,P_0)$, $q_k\sim N_{m_k}(0,Q_k)$, and $r_k\sim N_{p_k}(0,R_k)$ be mutually independent, with symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance matrices, where $C\succeq0$ means $z^TCz\ge0$ for every vector $z$ of matching dimension and $N_d(\mu,C)$ denotes the $d$-dimensional Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and covariance $C$, including singular $C$. Assume
$$a_k=F_ka_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad y_k=H_ka_k+r_k\quad(1\le k\le T).$$
Initialize $m_{0|0}=\mu_0$ and $P_{0|0}=P_0$. For $1\le k\le T$, define
$$m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1},\qquad P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k,$$
$$v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1},\qquad S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k.$$
Here $\mu_0\in\mathbb R^{m_0}$, $F_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times m_{k-1}}$, $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times m_k}$, $P_0\in\mathbb R^{m_0\times m_0}$, $Q_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times m_k}$, and $R_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times p_k}$. Assume every $S_k$ to be inverted is positive definite, meaning $z^TS_kz>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$. Set
$$K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1},\qquad m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k,\qquad P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T.$$
Write $y_{1:k}=(y_1,\ldots,y_k)$, let $y_{1:0}$ be the singleton empty history, and let $\nu_k$ be the probability law of $y_{1:k}$. For every $0\le k\le T$, the Gaussian kernel $\pi_k(y_{1:k},\cdot)=N_{m_k}(m_{k|k},P_{k|k})$ is a probability kernel from histories to coefficient-state laws and satisfies the regular-conditional-law identities: for every Borel state set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_k}$ and Borel history set $B\subseteq\prod_{j=1}^k\mathbb R^{p_j}$, $\mathbb P(a_k\in A,\ y_{1:k}\in B)=\int_B\pi_k(y,A)\,\nu_k(dy)$. For $k=0$, the history space is a singleton and $\pi_0=N_{m_0}(\mu_0,P_0)$. If $U_k=\Phi_k(a_k)$ is the represented velocity field, its regular conditional law is the pushforward kernel
$$\rho_k(y_{1:k},C)=\pi_k(y_{1:k},\Phi_k^{-1}(C))\qquad(C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)).$$
Both kernels are defined at every observation history, including histories with probability zero; this selects a version and asserts no pointwise uniqueness there. The result is exact for the declared finite model and does not assert that an untruncated or nonlinear fluid flow, an actual sensor, or actual noise follows that model.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC as required for the finite Gaussian-law construction and the exact filtering supplier. The sensor-to-coefficient identification and pushforward of the conditional law use no stronger choice principle.

title: Measurement and assimilation model adoption — Examples

items.title: One weighted sensor for one constant velocity mode
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the finite Gaussian-law construction in the adopted model. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable in SI spatial coordinates, with volume $V=|D|>0$ measured in m$^3$, and let $e\in\mathbb R^3$ be a fixed unit vector. Define the dimensionless constant modal field $\phi:D\to\mathbb R^3$ and the sensor weight $\psi:D\to\mathbb R^3$ by $\phi(x)=e$ and $\psi(x)=e/V$ for $x\in D$; the weight has units m$^{-3}$. Define the ideal weighted spatial sensor $S_\psi:L^2(D;\mathbb R^3)\to\mathbb R$ by
$$S_\psi(v):=\int_D v(x)\cdot\psi(x)\,d^3x.$$
Then $\phi,\psi\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^3)$ and $S_\psi(\phi)=1$, a dimensionless response. Let the scalar modal coefficient have prior law $a_0\sim N(\mu,P)$, where $N(\mu,P)$ denotes the scalar Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and variance $P$, including $P=0$, with $\mu$ in m s$^{-1}$ and $P\ge0$ in (m s$^{-1}$)$^2$. Set the dimensionless transition $F_1=1$, zero process covariance $Q_1=0$ in (m s$^{-1}$)$^2$, and zero process noise $q_1=0$ in m s$^{-1}$, so $a_1=F_1a_0+q_1=a_0$. Take observation noise $r_1\sim N(0,R)$ with $R>0$ in (m s$^{-1}$)$^2$, independent of $a_0$ and $q_1$. The represented velocity is $U_1(x)=a_1e$ for $x\in D$ and the single observation is $y_1=a_1+r_1$ in m s$^{-1}$. The exact one-step filter outputs
$$m_{1|1}=\mu+\frac{P}{P+R}(y_1-\mu),\qquad P_{1|1}=\frac{PR}{P+R}.$$
This is a symbolic model calculation, including the deterministic-prior case $P=0$; it records no measured fluid data.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC as in the finite Gaussian-law construction and the supplied conditional-filter result; the scalar calculation adds no choice principle.
